title: California is swimming in AI billions — but still faces an obscene budget black hole
excerpt: Governor-elect Xavier Becerra should recession-proof the state budget by cutting wasteful spending and paying money back into the rainy day fund.
content:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The good news for California is that the Anthropic IPO is going to bring billions into state coffers. The bad news is that we still might have a budget deficit.

That’s the opinion of the nonpartisan Legislative Analyst’s Office, which warned this week that Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra will face a $2 billion deficit next year, and possible future deficits of $15 billion every year after that.

One reason is that California depends on a small number of very high earners to pay the lion’s share of taxes. (Not exactly a “fair share,” either — a lot more than that.) 

When Wall Street has a bad year, Sacramento has a bad year. And the analysts are worried that there could be an “AI bust,” just like there was a dot-com bust over a quarter-century ago.

That points to the underlying problem: California’s government spends way too much money.

That’s why Gavin Newsom had to wrestle with deficits over the past two years — even though the AI boom had already begun.

It’s not a problem a “mileage tax” can ever solve.

California keeps expanding entitlement programs, and adding new ones. And in a one-party state, where the shrinking Republican Party can’t offer any opposition, there is no way to hold back the Democratic Party’s spending spree.

Gov. Jerry Brown imposed some fiscal discipline on the Legislature, and created the state’s rainy day fund for emergencies.

But Newsom raided that fund on his way out, dipping into $20 billion in savings so he could tell presidential primary voters in South Carolina that he had balanced California’s budget.

There was no “emergency” — other than the self-created fiscal dilemma Newsom faced after adding illegal immigrants to Medi-Cal, wasting billions on a failing high-speed rail project, and letting fraud run rampant in hospice funding and other programs. 

The Legislative Analyst’s Office could be wrong. The Anthropic IPO could give new energy to the AI boom, which seemed to have faltered in the wake of Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia amid allegations of inappropriate sexual relationships.

If that’s the case, California will benefit, and avoid yet another round of deficits. But if money continues rolling in, we should not waste the opportunity to put our fiscal house in order.

Gov.-elect Becerra should recession-proof the state budget by cutting wasteful spending and putting money back into the rainy-day fund.

That seems unlikely, but it’s the only responsible option.
